title: The RealReal makes it harder for shopping agents to hold the cart
friendlyTitle: A secondhand clothes site is blocking shopping agents at the cart
summary: The RealReal told The Verge it has tightened bot defenses so agents have a much harder time logging in, adding items to a cart, and checking out. The change follows a Verge test in which Meta's Muse kept re-adding listings as soon as a 20-minute hold expired, blocking other shoppers for hours. Agents can still surface listings and send a person to the product page. Meta did not comment.
friendlySummary: The RealReal told The Verge it has made it much harder for agents to log in, add items to a cart, and check out. The change follows a test in which Meta's Muse kept putting listings back in the cart as soon as a 20-minute hold ran out. That blocked other shoppers for hours. Agents can still show listings and send a person to the product page. Meta did not comment.
whyItMatters: A cart hold assumes a person who gets bored. An agent does not. If you shop secondhand, or you run a shop with a reserve timer, the practical change is already here: the agent may get you to the page and then stop. The Verge also notes Meta's claim that shopping was Muse's most common use, with purchases averaging over $200, and that 10 million people in the US had downloaded the app in 40 days.
